name: Question 10
problem:
The centers of two objects are separated by a distance of $(5.0\times {10}^{2})\,\text{m}$ and the magnitude of the gravitational force between them is $(7.2\times {10}^{-5})\,\text{N}.$ If one object has mass $(3.6\times {10}^{6})\,\text{kg},$ then according to Newton's law of universal gravitation, what is the mass of the other object? Write your answer in scientific notation, rounding to **two significant figures** where appropriate. Assume the Newtonian constant of gravitation is $G=(6.67\times {10}^{-11})\,{\text{m}}^{3}/(\text{kg}\cdot {\text{s}}^{2}).$

The mass of the other object is
$(${{field-1}}
$\times $
{{field-2}}$)\,\text{kg}.$
worked_solution:
Newton's law of universal gravitation states that the gravitational force attracting two objects is proportional to the product of the two masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between their centers of mass:

$$
F=G\frac{{m}_{1}{m}_{2}}{{r}^{2}}
$$

where

- $F$ is the gravitational force between the objects, measured in Newtons $(\text{N}),$

- $G=(6.67\times {10}^{-11})\,{\text{m}}^{3}/(\text{kg}\cdot {\text{s}}^{2})$ is the Newtonian constant of gravitation,

- ${m}_{1}$ and ${m}_{2}$ are the masses of the objects, measured in $\text{kg},$ and

- $r$ is the distance between their centers of mass, measured in $\text{m}.$

Let ${m}_{2}$ be the unknown mass.
First, let's rearrange the formula to make ${m}_{2}$ the subject:

$$
\begin{aligned}F & =G\frac{{m}_{1}{m}_{2}}{{r}^{2}} \\ F{r}^{2} & =G{m}_{1}{m}_{2} \\ {m}_{2} & =\frac{F{r}^{2}}{G{m}_{1}}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, substituting in the known values, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{m}_{2} & =\frac{(7.2\times {10}^{-5})\cdot (5.0\times {10}^{2})^{2}}{(6.67\times {10}^{-11})\cdot (3.6\times {10}^{6})} \\  & =\frac{7.2\cdot (5.0)^{2}}{6.67\cdot 3.6}\times \frac{{10}^{-5}\cdot ({10}^{2})^{2}}{{10}^{-11}\cdot {10}^{6}} \\  & =(7.496…)\times {10}^{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, rounded to two significant figures, the mass of the other object is
$(\,7.5\times {10}^{4}\,)\,\text{kg}.$

EXPLANATION

Newton's law of universal gravitation states that the gravitational force attracting two objects is proportional to the product of the two masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between their centers of mass: F=Gm1m2r2 where

  • F is the gravitational force between the objects, measured in Newtons (N),

  • G=(6.67×10−11)m3/(kg⋅s2) is the Newtonian constant of gravitation,

  • m1 and m2 are the masses of the objects, measured in kg, and

  • r is the distance between their centers of mass, measured in m.

Let m2 be the unknown mass. First, let's rearrange the formula to make m2 the subject:

F=Gm1m2r2Fr2=Gm1m2m2=Fr2Gm1

Then, substituting in the known values, we get

m2=(7.2×10−5)⋅(5.0×102)2(6.67×10−11)⋅(3.6×106)=7.2⋅(5.0)26.67⋅3.6×10−5⋅(102)210−11⋅106=(7.496…)×104.

Therefore, rounded to two significant figures, the mass of the other object is (7.5×104)kg.
